div.l: Vp on a day he gat hym more moneye
Than the ꝑpersoıı̄un gat / in monthes tweye
And thus with feyned flat̉ering and iapes
He made the ꝑpersoıı̄un / and the peple his apes
But trewely to tellen / at the laste
He was in chirche a noble ecclesiaste
Wel couthe he rede / a lessoıı̄un or a storie
But altherbest / he song an offretorie
For wel he wiste / whan that song was songe
He muste preche / and wel affile his tonge
To wynne siluer as he wel Cowde
Therfore he song / so merily and lowde
Now haue I tolde ȝow / sothely in a clause
The estate the array / the nombre and eke the cause
Why that assembled / was this companye
In Suthwerk / at this gentil hostelrye
That highte the tabbard / fast by the belle
But now is tyme / to ȝow for to telle
How that we baren vs / that ilke nyght
Whan we were / in that hostelrie a lyght
And after wol I tellen of oure viage
And al the remenant / of oure pilgrimage
But first I pray ȝow / of ȝoure curtesie
That ȝe ne rette it nought my vilenie
Though that I pleinly speke / in this mat̉ere
To tellen ȝow / h̉ere wordes / and her chere
Ne though I speke / her wordes proꝑperly
For this ȝe knowen as wel as I
Who so shal shall telle / a tale after a man
He moot reherse / as neygh as eủere he can
Eủery worde / ȝif it be in his charge
Al speke he neủere so rudely or large
Or elles he moot telle / his tale vntrewe
Or feyne thinges / or fynde wordes newe
He may nought spare / al though he were his brother
He moot as wel say / oo worde as a nother
Crist spak hym self / ful brode in holy writ
And wel ȝe woot / no vileny is it
Eke plato seith / who so can hym rede
